page.layout: Top: two coin engravings side by side, left and right, with no running text. Below them: one text block of two paragraphs, full width. Below the text: one printed ornament, no text. No margin notes.

main_text.l: CARINUS, Cæsar à patre dictus, omnibus se sceleribus
inquinavit: plurimos innoxios fictis criminibus occidit: matri-
monia nobilium corrupit. Ad extremū trucidatur, eius præci-
puè tribuni opera, & dextera, cuius dicebatur coniugē polluis-
NUMERIANUS Cæsar Carini frater, Carino tamen
longè absimilis fuit. hic nempe adolescens tum probitatis, tum
eruditionis eximiæ, maximè verò ad poëticen natus erat, atque
etiam ad arma. hic itaque miles, orator, poëta, dum oculis æger
in occlusa lectica ferretur, confecto bello Persico, unà cum patre,
ab Apro socero, Imperiū invadere cupiēte occiditur. Nec eius
mors inulta est, concionante Aprū Diocletianus manu propria
confodit. Imperarunt hi tres, Carus, Carinus & Numerianus,

page.notes: No marginal notes. The two coin engravings carry circular legends that are printed on the image: left "IMPERATOR CAES CARINVS NO[B]" (the last letters are cut off at the edge, so [?]); right "IMP NVMERIANVS AVG". These are not transcribed as main text. The ornament at the foot is decorative and has no text. The long s is read as plain s throughout. "Consulito" is read from the long-s form and may be a doubtful reading.
